label: to review
Proposed: Franken
research: The archival abstract identifies the sealer only as Hans von Rosenberg. The 1529-11-12.json couple lived at Mergentheim under Walter von Cronberg, and 1530-04-25.json names a Hans sealing a Neuhaus hospital matter; this makes the same Franken Hans plausible in the 1531 Neuhaus matter, but neither record establishes the sealer’s identity. Mönch and other same-name bearers remain possible; attribution is unresolved pending seal or other identifying evidence. Further charter comparisons support a tentative Franken attribution. In 1523-06-08.json Hans, bailiff of Röttingen, and Richezza sold revenues to the Amt Neuhaus, and the act mentions Althausen, the 1531 principals’ home. Cronberg’s two-year grant of a house in Mergentheim to Hans and Reytza in 1529-11-12.json covers January 1531. A Hans mediated a settlement involving Cronberg alongside Albrecht von Adelsheim in 1531-09-04.json and sealed a related Rengershausen transaction in 1532-06-03.json. These recurring local and personal ties favor the Franconian Hans, whom the Mainz regesta identify through his wife Ritz von Adelsheim and father Michel (https://www.ingrossaturbuecher.de/id/person/276). The detailed catalogue describes the single seal as lost (https://www2.landesarchiv-bw.de/ofs21/olf/druckansicht.php?id_titlaufn=3867887&bestand=17108).

entries.german:
Philipp Kempach, gesessen zu Althausen, und seine Ehefrau Otilia Schmidin begeben sich in Neuhaus zum Preis von 6 fl. rhen. mit ihren drei Kindern Klaus, Hans und Philipp in die Leibeigenschaft des Hochmeisters des Deutschen Ordens Walter von Cronberg, um der Armut zu entgehen.Philipp verpflichtet sich zusätzlich zusammen mit anderen Hintersassen des Spitals für zwei Tage im Jahr zum Dienst in den Weingütern am Sitz des Hochmeisters in Mergentheim.

Laufzeit: 1531 Januar 21 (Samstag nach Sebastiani)

Siegler: Hans von Rosenberg
entries.english:
Philipp Kempach, resident of Althausen, and his wife Otilia Schmidin, with their three children Klaus, Hans, and Philipp, enter into the serfdom of the Grand Master of the Teutonic Order, Walter von Cronberg, at Neuhaus for the price of 6 florins (Rhenish), in order to escape poverty.
Philipp additionally commits himself, together with other dependents of the hospital, to two days of service per year in the vineyards at the seat of the Grand Master in Mergentheim.

Date range: January 21, 1531 (Saturday after Sebastiani)

Seal: Hans von Rosenberg

facts.content: sealed the act in which Philipp Kempach and his family entered the serfdom of Deutschordens-Hochmeister Walter von Cronberg.
